# Garage AI

> Garage AI (GarageAI) is a two-sided marketplace for local AI inference in Europe. Garage owners ("operators") connect GPUs they already own and get paid per token for the requests they serve; buyers use open models through one OpenAI-compatible API. The principle: Europe's AI capacity can come from hardware people and companies already own, not only from hyperscaler data centres.

## Key facts (what works today)

- **For buyers:** Sign up at https://app.garageai.eu, create an API key and call the OpenAI-compatible API at https://llm.garageai.eu/v1 (works with OpenAI SDKs, agents and coding tools), or use the chat in the portal. Pay per token with prepaid credits (card via Stripe).
- **Pricing:** Each garage sets its own price per million tokens (input and output); GarageAI has no price list of its own. Buyers pay per token at the price of the garage that served the request.
- **Two ways to buy a model:** "Specific garage" (a named garage, e.g. for location; you pay its price) or "Pool" (one model name across every garage offering the model; each request goes to one healthy garage and is billed at that garage's price, with automatic failover). Both are shared, not exclusive, capacity.
- **For operators:** Sign up at https://app.garageai.eu/auth?intent=operator and follow the "Offer your GPU" wizard. Supported OS: macOS and Linux. Windows is in beta: a PowerShell connect script for Ollama and LM Studio (https://github.com/magnusfroste/garageai/blob/main/scripts/garageai-connect.ps1), tested in CI but not yet on a real GPU machine and not yet in the portal wizard; beta testers can email powerup@garageai.eu with the subject "Windows beta". Supported runtimes: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang and Paddock (beta). One command (the connect script, currently in beta) installs the NetBird client, joins the encrypted mesh and registers the models. Every model must pass an automated acceptance test (time-to-first-token, tokens/second) before it can be sold.
- **Operator earnings:** Operators set their own price and earn it for every token their garage serves, also for pool requests. No platform fee during launch (a fee will come later). Wallet and payouts are being built.
- **Technology (open source):** Self-hosted NetBird (WireGuard mesh) — no inbound ports, garages cannot reach each other, only the gateway reaches a runtime. LiteLLM gateway (OpenAI-compatible API, routing, failover, usage metering) on an EU VPS (Hetzner, Helsinki). The gateway does not reveal to buyers which garage served a request, and it automatically blocks clients that guess API keys or probe it.
- **Privacy, honestly:** Traffic is encrypted in transit over the mesh, but prompts are processed on the operator's machine. Verified garages and data-processing agreements are planned before selling to buyers with sensitive data.
- **GarageAI Bridge (experimental):** one binary, `garageai`, for Linux, macOS and Windows that will replace the connect script. Today it runs `garageai doctor` (what runs on the machine, what is wrong and how to fix it; never prompts, keys or command lines). Planned: connect, keep the garage running, pause it when the owner needs the GPU, and a local control panel. Roadmap: https://github.com/magnusfroste/garageai/blob/main/docs/bridge.md
- **Status:** Launched in 2026 after a private beta in spring 2026. Live, with the first garages serving open models.
- **License:** Open source, MIT.

## Vision (not today's product)

Garage nodes running largely on locally produced energy (rooftop solar, home batteries, EV batteries), many more garages across Europe, and larger regional clusters.
